title: Remove dead code from bun_format and napi.cpp
author: robobun
summary: - Two trait impls in `bun_format` have no user: `Spanned for FormatExpr` (`src/format/js/format.rs`) and `Spanned for FormatSpecifier` (`src/format/js/print/import_declaration.rs`). rustc's `dead_code` lint exempts trait impls, so the deny lints do not report them. - `Bun__napi_get_version` (`src/jsc/bindings/napi.cpp`) has no caller.

title: Bun.serve(http3): resolve stop() after the UDP socket and the last QUIC connection are gone
author: robobun
summary: - `await server.stop()` on an HTTP/3 server resolves while a QUIC connection drains and the UDP socket is bound. The next `Bun.serve` on that port throws `Failed to listen on UDP port N for HTTP/3`, and a process that ends there cuts the response in flight. - `stop_listening` took `h3_listener` (`src/runtime/server/mod.rs:1727`), so `is_closed()` (`mod.rs:1653`) had no HTTP/3 term.

title: install.sh: write ~/.bashrc first on Linux and skip files that already have the bun block
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44945 - On Linux with both `~/.bash_profile` and `~/.bashrc` present, the installer writes only `~/.bash_profile` and reports `Added "~/.bun/bin" to $PATH in "~/.bash_profile"`. A new terminal then says `bash: bun: command not found`. A Linux terminal opens an interactive non-login shell, which reads only `~/.bashrc`. - The cause is the file order in `src/runtime/cli/install.sh:269` (`bash_configs`). #11679 put `~/.bash_profile` first on every OS to fix macOS (#1897), where Terminal opens

title: bun patch --help: add --commit to the custom patches directory example
author: robobun
summary: - The third example of `bun patch --help` is `bun patch --patches-dir 'my-patches' 'node_modules/jquery'`. Its description is "Generate a patch file in a custom directory for changes made to jquery". Run as printed on an edited folder, it exits 0, writes no patch file, and the edit is gone. - The example lacks `--commit`. Without `--commit`, `bun patch` puts a fresh copy of the package in the folder and never reads `--patches-dir` (`src/install/PackageManager/CommandLineArguments.rs:1626`).

title: node:fs: fs.Dir reads from a native directory stream
author: robobun
summary: - `fs.opendir()` opens nothing. The first `read()` lists the whole directory by path with one `fs.readdir()` (`src/js/node/fs.ts:1143`), or the whole tree with `recursive: true`. - So a `Dir` reads a directory that was renamed into its path, or throws `ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir` after `rm`. One unreadable directory deep in a tree fails the first recursive read with `EACCES`.

title: bun:dom and the Vitest work in one tree (not for merging)
author: Jarred-Sumner
summary: Not for merging. It puts two branches in one tree so that CI makes a build of both to try: - #44833, the Vitest compatibility work for `bun test`. Its change to `setTimeout(callback, 0)` is off here unless `BUN_TEST_ZERO_DELAY_TIMERS=1` is set, so that one build can be timed both ways. - `bun:dom`, a DOM built into Bun (WebKit's DOM and HTML parser, without loading, layout and rendering), which will get a pull request of its own On top of the two there is a test environment for the built-in DOM:

title: node:stream: finish the decoder in `setEncoding()` when the stream has ended
author: robobun
summary: - `Readable#setEncoding()` on a stream that already holds its data and its end drops the end of the text. The reader gets a shorter text, `'end'`, no error. - `setEncoding` (`src/js/internal/streams/readable.ts:520`) decodes the buffered chunks with a new `StringDecoder` and never calls `decoder.end()`. Only `push(null)` calls it, through `onEofChunk` (`:710`). - One `await` before `res.setEncoding('base64')` is enough. Bun 1.3.14 returns the whole text there.

title: redis: send HELLO once when a TLS 1.2 server renegotiates
author: robobun
summary: - A TLS 1.2 server renegotiates between a command and its reply. `Bun.RedisClient` then sends `HELLO 3 AUTH <user> <password>` again. The server answers it, so every later command gets the reply to the command before it: `get c` returns `{ server: "redis", proto: 3 }`. - A renegotiation ends in a second handshake report. `on_handshake` (`src/runtime/valkey_jsc/js_valkey.rs:1862`) calls `start()` for each report, and `start()` writes `HELLO`.

title: html dev server: keep serving when `o + Enter` cannot launch the opener
author: robobun
summary: Part of #26231 - `bun ./index.html`, then `o` + Enter: if the opener cannot be launched, the dev server exits with code 1. On Windows the opener is `start`, which is not a program: every press ends the server with `error: Executable not found in $PATH: "start"` (#26231, #32513). So does Linux without `xdg-open`. - Cause: `Bun.spawn` throws synchronously in the stdin `data` listener, and the arm guards only `.exited` (`src/js/internal/html.ts:387-395`).

title: sql(mysql): send XA ROLLBACK after a refused XA END on a rolled-back branch
author: robobun
summary: - After a deadlock (1213) or a MariaDB write conflict (1020) inside `sql.beginDistributed()`, the server refuses `XA END` (`XA_RBDEADLOCK`, or `XAER_RMFAIL: The command cannot be executed when global transaction is in the ROLLBACK ONLY state`). `end()` (`src/js/bun/sql.ts:504`) stops there: no `XA ROLLBACK`. - The pool closes that connection only while its status flag shows a transaction. One statement that opens no table clears it, and the next caller gets the branch. A reservation always keeps

title: node:fs: resolve a relative path that normalizes to nothing to the cwd on Windows
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #45059 - On Windows, `fs.mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true })` throws `ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir` with an empty path for `p` in `./`, `.\`, `sub/..`. For `.` it throws `EEXIST`. `fs.promises.mkdir` and the callback form fail the same way. `fs.existsSync` returns `false` for the same inputs. Node and Deno return `undefined` and `true`. - The cause is `PathLikeExt::os_path_kernel32` (`src/runtime/node/types.rs:1072`). It normalizes a relative path before it hands it to kernel32.

title: bundler: resume the shared resolve pass for imports that went to onResolve plugins
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #19951, fixes #22838 - An import or entry point that matches an `onResolve` filter builds differently, also when every callback returns nothing. Example: `Could not resolve: "react/jsx-dev-runtime"`. - `run_resolver` (`src/bundler/bundle_v2.rs:2651` on main) resolves a declined import. It is a hand copy of `resolve_import_records`. `on_resolve` makes the module of an answered import itself. Both miss rules of the shared pass, for example the tsconfig JSX settings.

title: Link ContextDestructionObservers intrusively so a context's destructor drains them in linear time
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44898 - `bun test --parallel` (implies `--isolate`) stalls at 100% CPU for minutes in `ScriptExecutionContext::~ScriptExecutionContext`, inside `HashSet::takeAny` -> `skipEmptyBuckets` (`src/jsc/bindings/ScriptExecutionContext.cpp:220`). - `takeAny()` rescans from bucket 0 past the tombstones of every earlier call: O(N^2) in the observers still registered. Under `--isolate` the retired global dies before the wrappers of the AbortSignals, EventTargets and ports its file left alive are swep

title: `bun lint --staged` and `bun fmt --staged` read what is staged
author: Jarred-Sumner
summary: With `--staged`, git only chose which files to look at. Their text still came from the disk. So a file with both staged and unstaged changes (`git add -p`, or an edit after `git add`) was judged by code that the commit doesn't get. | Case | Before | Now | | --- | --- | --- | | `debugger` is staged, then removed on disk | `bun lint --staged` says "No problems" and the commit gets it | Reported, at its place in the staged text | | The staged version is clean, `debugger` is only on disk | The commi

title: Remove dead code from bun_format, bun_sema, bun_install, and bun_core
author: robobun
summary: - Nine trait impls, one function and one generated method have no user. `rustc`'s `dead_code` lint exempts trait impls and `pub` items, so the deny lints do not report them. - They are: six `Spanned` impls in `bun_format`, `Default for Session` and `Files::default_of_module` in `bun_sema`, `PartialEq<crate::Error> for ForTarballError` and `Display for Id` in `bun_install`, and `StoredTrace::from` in `bun_core`. - `bun_lint_react` lists `bun_glob` as a dependency and does not use it.

title: Blob: a copy of a File is a plain Blob (file.slice(), new Blob([file]), response.blob())
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #43691 Part of #35439. Stacked on #45373. - `file.slice()` returns a `File` with the whole file's `name` and `lastModified`, so each upload chunk goes out as `filename="report.pdf"`. The File API returns a plain `Blob`. - `Blob::dupe_with_content_type` (`src/jsc/webcore_types.rs:356`) copies `is_jsdom_file`, `name` and `last_modified`. `get_slice_from` (`src/runtime/webcore/Blob.rs:1800`), `new Blob([file])` and `response.blob()` use that copy.

title: uws: key HttpRouter by method id
author: robobun
summary: - `HttpRouter::route()` finds the tree of a method with a scan over the method names. A `POST` costs 291 instructions more than a `GET`. - When no tree has the name, `route()` takes `root.children.back()` (`packages/bun-uws/src/HttpRouter.h:276`). That is the any-method node only while no removal erased it. #45396 and #45397 keep requests away from that line. - Each request resolves its method twice: for the 501 check and for `Request::method()`.

title: server: read the method id uWS resolved, not the method name
author: robobun
summary: - A route handler asks uWS for the method name and looks it up in `METHOD_MAP`. 12 readers handle a failed lookup. 10 of them substitute `GET`, `POST` or `OPTIONS` (`RequestContext.rs:1426`, `DevServer.rs:1774`). - With #45396 and #45357 no handler runs for a name that is not in the map, so the arms cannot run.

title: node:http: keep the method of a dispatched request as sent in 'clientError' rawPacket
author: robobun
summary: - node:http: the `rawPacket` of a `'clientError'` shows an earlier request of the same read with a lowercase method, `get /a HTTP/1.1`. Node.js shows the bytes as the client sent them. - `HttpRequest::getMethod()` (`packages/bun-uws/src/HttpParser.h:539`) lowercases the method in the receive buffer when a handler reads it. `rawPacket` is that buffer.

title: Bun.serve: register the default handler on "/*" for every method
author: robobun
summary: - Under `"/*": { GET: fn }`, `PROPFIND /x` gets the 404 of a router miss and not `fetch`. Under `"/*": { GET: static, TRACE: fn }` the `TRACE` handler runs. - `set_routes` (`src/runtime/server/mod.rs:2677`) registers the default handler per other method with `App::method()`, which knows 9 of the 36 methods (`src/uws_sys/App.rs:227`). - That loop also replaces the `HEAD` of a non-function `GET` route.

title: Bun.serve: answer 501 to an unknown method and 404 to a router miss, not a closed socket
author: robobun
summary: Part of #6556 and #18406 - An HTTP/1.1 request with an unknown method (`BREW`, `get`) closes the socket with no response. On some route tables a handler runs and sees `req.method === "GET"`. - `HttpRouter::route()` (`packages/bun-uws/src/HttpRouter.h:276`) falls back to `root.children.back()`. A repeated registration erases the empty any-method node, so that is another method's tree. - Behind nginx, one `BREW /` gives 502 to every client for about 10 s (Notes).

title: node:fs: return readdir entries in strcmp order like node
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44947, fixes #25734 - `fs.readdirSync`, `fs.readdir` and `fs.promises.readdir` return entries in kernel order. Node returns each directory's entries in `strcmp` order on Unix: libuv's `uv_fs_scandir` sorts them. Programs that depend on that order (Metro asset resolution, React Native codegen, index builders) give different output under Bun. - The three readdir loops in `src/runtime/node/node_fs.rs` (`readdir_with_entries`, `readdir_with_entries_recursive_sync`, `readdir_with_entries_recur

title: Embed files named by new URL(relative, import.meta.url) in bun build --compile
author: robobun

The binary fails with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/$bunfs/root/data.bin'`. author: robobun

title: Bun.Image: build the PNG palette by squared error, with cuts between colour values
author: robobun
summary: - `png({ palette: true, colors: 2 })` on a 75% white, 25% black image writes `(128,128,128)`, `(255,255,255)`: mid grey for black. - Cause: main (`src/runtime/image/quantize.rs:112`) cuts each box of pixels at its pixel-count midpoint. A colour with over half of the box lands in both halves.

title: test: treat AGENT as a boolean and detect agents from AI_AGENT
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44459, fixes #44418 - `AGENT=crush bun test` and `AI_AGENT=pi bun test` print the human output. `AGENT=crush CLAUDECODE=1 bun test` does too. Only `AGENT=1`, `CLAUDECODE=1` and `REPL_ID=1` turn the quiet output on. - The cause is `is_ai_agent()` in `src/bun_core/output.rs:857`. `AGENT` is a string env var and the check is `env == b"1"`. author: robobun

title: EventTarget: remove a { signal } listener without a scan of its AbortSignal
author: robobun
summary: - Removing a `{ signal }` listener scans every other listener of that `AbortSignal`. 80,000 listeners on one signal take 1.7 s to remove, 15 ms without it. summary: Fixes #44925 - After the client disconnects, `res.end("late")` sets `res._header` but leaves `res.headersSent` false. `res.setHeader()` then throws `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` (`node:_http_outgoing`, `setHeader`). author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44642 **Status: waits for #44833.** That draft adds `[test] environment`, `--environment` and the `@jest-environment` / `@vitest-environment` docblocks, switches the DOM per file without `--isolate`, and makes the builtins immune to DOM globals. title: node:fs: do rm's directory check natively, so fs.rm(path, cb) throws invalid arguments from the call
author: robobun

Invalid options and recursive `fs.rmdir` have the same defect. - Cause: `src/js/node/fs.ts:107`. Since #31830, `fs.rm` calls the async `fs.promises.rm`, so a thrown error becomes a rejection. author: steipete

Follow [Node 24.21's cleanup order](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.21.0/lib/internal/worker.js#L385-L402): remove `message` and `messageerrors` before `exit`, unref the public port, and clean up user callbacks after exit handlers return. The plural `messageerrors` matc

title: FormData: name an unnamed Blob entry "blob", and let the filename argument name a File entry
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #14725 Part of #43691 and #35439. - `fd.append("f", new Blob(["x"]))` serializes as `filename=""`. The spec, Node and browsers send `filename="blob"`. Strict servers reject the part. - `fd.append("f", file, "renamed.txt")` keeps the File's own name on the value that `fd.get()` returns. - `JSDOMFormData.cpp:311` defaults the entry filename to the Blob's name or an empty string. `Blob__setAsFile` (`src/runtime/webcore/Blob.rs:3997`) applies it only to a Blob with no name.

title: shell: keep variables in one table with an export attribute, and prefix assignments on their command
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #32202 - `T=5; export T; printenv T` prints an empty line. `HOME=/tmp/zz env` prints two `HOME=` lines. `PATH=/x:$PATH; tool` fails with `bun: command not found: tool`. - Three maps hold values, and "exported" means "in `export_env`". `export NAME` writes `""` there (`builtin/export.rs:35`), and `NAME=v` writes only `shell_env` (`interpreter.rs:2153`). Each spawn appends `cmd_local_env`, which no command clears (`states/Cmd.rs:486`).

title: Bun.Image: dither error shares add up, and the error is measured inside 0..255
author: robobun
summary: - `png({ palette: true, dither: true })` speckles flat areas that have their own palette entry. On `docs/images/guides/lambda1.png` at 256 colours, 4,726,170 flat pixels come back as another entry. - `map_floyd_steinberg` (`src/runtime/image/quantize.rs:237-244`) floors each of the four error shares: an error of -1 pushes -4, and +1 pushes 0. It also takes the error from the unclamped candidate (`:231`), so a colour outside the palette's range adds error that nothing absorbs.

title: Run runtime plugin onResolve for a specifier without an extension
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44603, fixes #40579 - A runtime plugin's `onResolve` never runs for a package name (`@somemodule/foo`), an extension-less path (`./other`), or `virtual:thing` under a file-namespace filter. The import fails with `Cannot find module '@somemodule/foo'`. - Cause: the `could_be_plugin` pre-filter in `plugin_namespace_and_path` (`src/jsc/ModuleLoader.rs:247`), checked by `run_on_resolve` (`src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs:7746`).

title: pm pkg get, pm view: append the found values without a lookup per member
author: robobun
summary: - `bun pm pkg get arr.q` on a package.json whose `arr` holds 64,000 objects takes 5.0 s. It grows 4 times when the array doubles. The review of #45061 found this. - `exec_get` (`src/runtime/cli/pm_pkg_command.rs:240`) calls `E::Object::put` for each found value. `put` searches the members that the object holds (`src/ast/e.rs:1398`), so N values cost N(N-1)/2 comparisons. `bun pm view --json` has the same loop with `Expr::set` (`pm_view_command.rs:397`).

title: structured-clone: stop decoding zero bytes to null
author: robobun
summary: - `v8.deserialize()` and `bun:jsc` `deserialize()` return `null` for zero bytes. Node throws. A zero-length advanced IPC frame arrives as a `null` message. - `postMessage([1, 2, 3])` delivers `null` when the receiver has an indexed accessor on `Array.prototype`. - Cause: `CloneDeserializer::deserialize` (`src/jsc/bindings/webcore/SerializedScriptValue.cpp:2275`) answers an empty buffer with `(jsNull(), UnspecifiedError)`. No caller throws for it.

title: toml: name the invalid escape and the literal-string fix in the error message
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #45036 - `Bun.TOML.parse('v = "C:\\Users\\name"')` throws `TOML Parse error: A Unicode escape must be followed by exactly 8 hex digits`. The user reads that as a hex formatting problem. The real rule is that `\U` starts an escape and a lone backslash is not allowed in a basic string. - `v = "\d+"` throws `Invalid escape sequence: 'd'`, with no hint at the fix. Both messages come from `scan_escape` and `read_hex_codepoint` in `src/parsers/toml.rs`.

title: css: fold relative colors on the scale of their function, and keep them as written when the fold is not exact
author: robobun
summary: - `bun build` prints invalid CSS when the unresolved alpha of a relative `rgb()` names a channel: `rgb(from #336699 r g b / calc(alpha * var(--o)))` becomes `rgb(51 102 153/calc(alpha*var(--o)))`. - A keyword is on the wrong scale: `rgb(from #336699 calc(r + 10) g b)` prints `#f69`.

title: fs.promises: FileHandle.writer() gives its ref back when a write rejects, and end()/fail() still run
author: robobun
summary: - After a `write()` of `FileHandle.writer()` rejects, `handle.close()` never settles and the handle stays locked. `pipeTo()` of `node:stream/iter` hits this. - The catch arms of `writeAll()` and `writevAll()` (`src/js/node/fs.promises.ts:1170`, `:1220`) set the `error` of `fail()` and run no teardown. The terminal calls (`end()`, `endSync()`, `fail()`, the disposers) then return before the unref and the unlock.

title: Bun.serve: apply server.timeout() on a unix socket server
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #43816 - `server.timeout(req, seconds)` returns `null` and does nothing when `Bun.serve` listens on a unix socket. `idleTimeout` stays in force, so the server cuts a quiet event stream that called `server.timeout(req, 0)`. - The cause is an early return for unix sockets in `timeout()` (`src/runtime/server/server_body.rs:1629`), before it sets the timer. #17093 added it with no comment.

title: node:crypto: take the default RSA padding for a falsy `padding` option
author: robobun
summary: - `crypto.publicEncrypt`, `privateDecrypt`, `privateEncrypt` and `publicDecrypt` throw `ERR_OSSL_EVP_ILLEGAL_OR_UNSUPPORTED_PADDING_MODE` when the key object has `padding: null`, `0`, `-0`, `false`, `NaN` or `""`. `padding: 0n` throws a `TypeError`. Node v26.3.0 takes the default padding for all seven. - The cause is `rsaFunction` (`src/jsc/bindings/node/crypto/JSCipher.cpp:87`). It skips the option only when it is `undefined`. Each other value goes to `toInt32`, which gives 0, and 0 is not a pa

title: node:module: report a script that Module.runMain() starts and that fails
author: robobun
summary: - A script started with `Module.runMain(path)` that throws, rejects a top-level await, or fails to parse or resolve exits 0 with empty stderr. Node exits 1. - `jsFunctionRunMain` (`NodeModuleModule.cpp:804`) gave the load promise to `set_override_module_run_main_promise` (`hw_exports.rs:108`), which dropped it unless the entry point's slot was empty. JSC marks it handled, so nobody reported it. - No user reported it. Corepack and `istanbul cover` make this call.

title: Bun.serve http3: 501 or 400 before the router for a request line the HTTP/2 listener refuses
author: robobun
summary: - `Bun.serve({ http3: true })` routes every request line. `:method: BREW` runs `fetch` as `GET`, and a static route serves it. - `:path: /guar<HTAB>ded` reaches `fetch` as `/guarded`, past the `/guarded` route. - Cause: the `on_stream_headers` callback (`packages/bun-uws/src/Http3Context.h:40`) calls the router with no check. The HTTP/2 listener refuses these lines since #40676.

title: util.inspect: print the state of Response, Request, Headers, Blob and six more classes
author: robobun
summary: - `util.inspect(new Response("x"))` returns `Response {}`. `Request`, `Headers`, `FormData`, `Blob`, `File`, `AbortSignal`, `AbortController`, `Event`, `TextDecoder` and `Timeout` print empty too. So does `console.log` in a `node:worker_threads` Worker. - Their state is in native fields. `formatValue` (`src/js/internal/util/inspect.js:1242`) prints own properties or calls `value[Symbol.for("nodejs.util.inspect.custom")]`, which node has and Bun did not. - This revives #35292.

title: Throw for a `file:` URL whose path is not UTF-8 on Linux and macOS, through one `fileSystemPath()` accessor
author: robobun
summary: - On Linux and macOS, a `file:` URL whose percent-decoded path is not UTF-8 (`file:///tmp/50%deposit.db`) converts to the path `""`. `Bun.SQL` then opens `:memory:`, `new Worker(url)` runs `./index.js`, and `createRequire(url)` resolves from the current directory. - `WTF::URL::fileSystemPath()` returns a null `String` for such a path. #46021 took the crash fix from this PR (`Segmentation fault at address 0x10`). 8 readers in `src/jsc` still take the null for `""`.

title: Standard decorators: keep a decorated #private member a member of the class
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #31910 - A standard decorator on a `#private` member breaks 26 of 31 uses. `this.#count++` gives `SyntaxError: Postfix ++ operator applied to value that is not a reference.` - `lower_class_body` (`src/js_parser/lower/lower_decorators.rs`) replaced the name with a WeakMap. A second pass, `rewrite_private_accesses_*`, rewrote each use. It knew four forms.

title: Evict a CommonJS module that failed during import by its require.cache key
author: robobun
summary: - An imported CommonJS module that assigns `module.filename` and then throws stays in `require.cache`. The next `require()` returns its `{}` exports. The entry under the assigned name is removed instead. - The loader's generator in `commonJSModuleSyntheticSourceCode` removed `module.filename` as read after the body ran (`JSCommonJSModule.cpp:1716`).

title: sys: end the listing of a directory that is removed while it is read
author: robobun
summary: - In a removed working directory, `fs.readdirSync(".")` throws `ENOENT scandir` (node: `[]`). `rm -rf **/node_modules` through `Bun.$` fails with `rm: <path>: No such file or directory` in 30 of 100 runs. - Linux answers `getdents64` with ENOENT once a directory is removed. glibc and musl `readdir` report the end. Both directory iterators return the errno (`src/sys/lib.rs`, `src/runtime/node/dir_iterator.rs`).

title: node:net: refuse connect() where node's handle refuses it
author: robobun
summary: - A `connect()` on a `net.Socket` whose handle still owns a socket resets that connection with no event and dials again. Node v26.3.0 refuses most such calls: `EALREADY` in flight, `EISCONN` for an accepted socket and after `end()`, `EINVAL` for a path on a TCP socket. - `connect_finish` calls `detach_for_reconnect` for every handle (`src/runtime/socket/Listener.rs:1613`, #32739). Found by a fuzz run, not by a user.

author: robobun
summary: - `bun build` removes `!ns;` and then drops every export of the `import()` target: `const ns = await import("./lib.js"); !ns; console.log(Object.keys(ns))` prints `[]`. - A CommonJS file with a removed `if (module.exports.a) {}` loses its wrapper while it still uses `module`: `ReferenceError: module_lib is not defined`. - `clear_symbol_usages_from_dead_part` (`src/js_parser/p.rs`) takes back a removed statement's uses. The two counts that `parse_entry.rs` compares with them keep its share (#3255

title: node:quic: open a uni stream requested before the handshake, keep pending streams paired with lsquic's requests
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44749 - `createUnidirectionalStream()` before the handshake completes loses that stream, and each later uni stream opens one request late. Node delivers all. - `lsquic_conn_make_uni_stream` (`patches/lsquic/node-quic-accessors.patch`) drops a request before the handshake. Its entry in `QuicSession::pending_local_uni` takes the next stream. - A destroyed pending stream keeps its lsquic request. It later takes a peer credit, and streams hang.

title: PerformanceObserver: observe Node's entry types in the global class, with one queue per observer
author: robobun
summary: - `node:perf_hooks` exports a JS subclass of `PerformanceObserver` that keeps Node's entry types (`function`, `net`, `http`, `http2`, `quic`) in a second queue, `NodeEntryObserver` (`src/js/internal/shared.ts:332`). - For these types `takeRecords()` returns `[]`, a later `disconnect()` loses the entries, the callback has no `this`, and the global class gets nothing.

title: shell: remove only trailing line ends from a quoted command substitution
author: robobun
summary: Stacked on #44752. - A quoted substitution in a command word drops every trailing space, tab and CR of the output. `echo "a$(printf ' ')b"` prints `ab`, bash prints `a b`. - `echo hi > "$(echo 'out ')"` writes `out`, and `cut -d"$(printf '\t')"` fails. - Cause: the trim loop in `Expansion::child_done` (`src/runtime/shell/states/Expansion.rs:650`). POSIX 2.6.3 removes only trailing newlines.

title: node:fs: finish a short write in fs.write and fs.writev the way libuv does
author: robobun
summary: - `fs.writeSync(1, text)` into a slow pipe returns 65536 of 4194304 bytes when a signal arrives (a `SIGCHLD` listener, `bun --cpu-prof`). No error, exit code 0. Node v26.3.0 writes all. - The four write arms in `src/runtime/node/node_fs.rs` return the count of the first `write(2)`. Linux also caps one write at 0x7ffff000 bytes.

title: console: `%s` prints a Symbol and an object that `String()` cannot convert
author: robobun
summary: - `console.log("%s", value)` throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a symbol to a string` for a Symbol and `TypeError: No default value` for an object with no `toString` (RegExp `groups`, `util.parseArgs().values`, `Object.groupBy()`). - The `%s` arm (`src/jsc/ConsoleObject.rs:2421`) sends every value to the engine ToString.

title: bun:ffi: build the Windows dlopen error text without a discarded write
author: robobun
summary: - mordant `discarded_error` flags `src/runtime/ffi/mod.rs:110` on the Windows target: "`.ok();` converts this `Result` to an `Option` and drops it, so the `std::io::Error` error disappears in a line that looks like handling". title: node:test: copy node's fixed method list onto t.assert
author: robobun
summary: - `t.assert` has an `Assert` key that Node does not have. `t.assert.Assert()` throws "Class constructor Assert cannot be invoked without `new`". - `buildContextAssert` (`src/js/node/test.ts`) copied every callable export of `node:assert` except a denylist, and #34660 added the `Assert` class. author: robobun

author: QQSHI13

author: dylan-conway
summary: `process.stdout.write("", cb)` ran `cb` at once even while earlier chunks were still waiting for a full pipe, so exiting from the callback lost them: ```sh bun -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(4 << 20)); process.stdout.write("", () => process.exit(0))' | (sleep 1; wc -c) # 1.4.3: 65536 this PR and node: 4194304 ``` **Cause.** `FileSink.write()` returns a promise while the sink is backed up and a number otherwise. title: FileSink: end the writer before the parked promise settles
author: robobun
summary: - `await proc.stdin.end()` returns with the pipe open. The repro prints `BLOCKED 3000 ms: the pipe is still open after await end()`. - `FileSink::on_write` (`src/runtime/webcore/FileSink.rs:428`) settled the parked promise, ran its reactions, then ended the writer. - The promise also settled with its bytes still buffered: from a task an earlier flush queued, or when a small `write()` followed.

title: node:http2: hold a response to its content-length
author: robobun
summary: - A `node:http2` client delivers response DATA past the declared `content-length`. An h2-to-h1 proxy forwards the excess, and the next hop reads it as a second response. A short body ends with `'end'` and `rstCode` 0. Node fails both (RFC 9113 section 8.1.1). - The engine checks requests only: `enforce_content_length` (`src/runtime/api/bun/h2/connection.rs:1709`) returns early on a client.

title: Bun.Image: copy the pipeline once per terminal and carry it across a Blob read
author: robobun
summary: - Outputs started together from one `Bun.file(path).image()` all get the last call's settings: `Promise.all([32, 16, 8].map(w => img.resize(w, w).png().bytes()))` silently resolves `8x8 8x8 8x8`. - `Image::schedule` (`src/runtime/image/Image.rs:1113`) sends a `Source::Blob` to `BlobReadChain` before the pipeline copy (`:1132`), which runs after the read (`:1353`). - The format travels from the call in `Kind::Encode`: `img.jpeg().bytes()` then `img.png().resize(8, 8)` resolves a JPEG at 8x8.

title: node:module: resolve compile cache env vars from process.env at call time
author: robobun

A `.env` line, a `--preload` script, or a `process.env` write before a tool (eslint, vite, tsc) enables the cache returns `{status: 1}` and populates the cache directory. Node returns `{status: 3, message: "Disabled by NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE"}` in all three cases. - The cause is `enable()` in `src/jsc/NodeCompileCache.rs:337` (and `:360`, `:288`, `:380`). author: robobun

title: worker: take a listener's termination at the native boundary, end the tick pass on a stopped VM
author: robobun
summary: - After `process.exit()` in a worker's `'uncaughtException'` listener, queued ticks and microtasks still run (since #42590, 1.4.3). `worker.terminate()` never settles when it lands in a listener of `dispatchEvent()`, `abort()` or `process.emit()`. Node stops in both. - `EventEmitter.cpp:260` and two more dispatchers called the listener through JSC's `NakedPtr<Exception>` overload, which clears a TerminationException. The tick loop (`JSNextTickQueue.cpp:106`) called the next tick after a report.

title: bundler: keep a read off a require() / import() local a property access until the linker binds it
author: robobun

For `const x_1 = require("./x")`, `(0, x_1.f)()` prints `x_1.f()` under `--minify-syntax`. `(1 && x_1.f)()` prints it with no flag. - An unused getter read `ns.a;` is removed. - The cause is `maybe_rewrite_property_access` (`src/js_parser/fold.rs`). It made `ns.f` an import item before the linker knew if it binds.

title: shell: flush the pending word in eat_subshell, so text before a backtick substitution stays in its word

author: robobun

title: node-fallbacks: treat ws: and wss: as slashed protocols in the url polyfill
author: robobun

title: fix(tls): omit implicit SNI for absent and null servernames
author: steipete
summary: Fixes `tls.connect({ host: "127.0.0.1", port, servername: null })` sending the IP address as TLS SNI. This can break servers that reject IP literals and clients such as undici that intentionally clear a TLS identity on a cross-origin request or redirect. The socket and secure-context names were combined with `||`, but the fallback guard only handled `undefined`. A `null` name therefore reached native TLS without an explicit empty name, allowing the native connection-host fallback to send the IP.

title: node:dns: disable the c-ares query cache

summary: - `formData()` on a Response or Request over `Bun.file()` resolves an empty FormData and never reads the file. Node parses the same body from `fs.openAsBlob()`. - A multipart file rejects with `FormData parse error missing final boundary`. `Bun.file(p).stream()` as the body parsed in 1.3 and is empty since 1.4.0. - Cause: `get_form_data` (`src/runtime/webcore/Body.rs:2130`) parses `blob.slice()` at once. That slice is empty when the bytes are on disk or in S3.

title: css: keep the namespace prefix on attribute selectors that have an operator
author: robobun
summary: - `bun build` drops the namespace prefix of an attribute selector with an operator and a lowercase name: `[xl|href$=".pdf"]` prints as `[href$=".pdf"]`, a different selector. - The two then compare equal, so every build mode deletes a rule: `[xl|href="a"]{color:red}[href="a"]{color:blue}` prints only `[href="a"]{color:#00f}`. - Cause: `namespace.is_some() && !local_name_is_ascii_lowercase` in `parse_attribute_selector` (`src/css/selectors/parser.rs:3532`). Only that arm keeps the namespace.

title: node:net: half-close an adopted socket fd one tick after end()
author: robobun
summary: - `end()` on `new net.Socket({ fd, writable: true, readable: false })` over a stream socket issues no `shutdown(2)`. The peer gets end-of-file only when `destroy()` closes the fd: never on a shared socket or an undestroyed stream. - Cause: `Socket.prototype._final` (`src/js/node/net.ts:2575`) calls back at once without a `_handle`. Node shuts down there. No issue reports this.

title: structuredClone: copy plain objects and arrays without serializing them
author: sosukesuzuki
summary: `structuredClone(value)` serialized the value and deserialized the result, except for a flat object or a flat array. A value that holds an object inside an object, which is most of them, paid for both passes: `structuredClone({ a: { b: 1 }, list: [1, 2] })` took over a microsecond. A value made only of plain objects, arrays, strings and other primitives is now copied object by object, with no serialized form in between. An object held twice, or one that holds itself, is cloned once, as before. T

title: nix: add packages.bun to the flake
author: asinglesprinkle
summary: Adds `packages.bun` and `packages.default` to `flake.nix`, so Nix users can install Bun from this repo: ```sh nix run github:oven-sh/bun -- --version nix profile install github:oven-sh/bun ``` Closes #40524. The package installs the release zips and doesn't build from source. Its derivation in `nix/package.nix` is based on the one in nixpkgs. On Linux, `autoPatchelfHook` patches the binary. On macOS, the ICU path is rewritten and the binary is re-signed. The package also links `bunx` to `bun` an

title: css: print `none` instead of an empty border-image, mask-border or mask-box-image value
author: robobun
summary: - `bun build` prints `border-image: none` as `border-image:` (`.btn.plain{border-image:}`). A browser drops that declaration, so the element keeps an earlier border image. - Cause: `BorderImage::to_css_internal` (`src/css/properties/border_image.rs:152`) prints a component only when it differs from its initial value, so five initial components print nothing. `mask-border` and `mask-box-image` share it.

title: test: fix the race in the two no-orphans Ctrl-Z tests
author: dylan-conway
summary: Fixes the two flaky Ctrl-Z tests in `test/cli/run/no-orphans.test.ts`. The file flaked in 55 of 569 CI builds from Oct 8 to Oct 13, with three symptoms. No runtime code changes. **Cause.** `bun run --no-orphans` puts the script in its own process group and then makes that group the terminal's foreground group (`JobControl::give` in `src/spawn/process.rs`). It does this after the spawn returns, so the script can already be running. Both tests took the script's first output as proof that the scrip

title: lexer: end a JSX pragma value at a line break in block comments too
author: robobun
summary: - A JSX pragma on its own line of a `/* */` comment keeps the line break in its value. `bun format --insert-pragma` writes that form. Then `@jsxImportSource ./my` fails with `Cannot find module './my\n/jsx-dev-runtime'`. - The value loop of `PragmaArg::scan` (`src/js_parser/lexer.rs:3552`) stops at a line break only for `//` comments. Fuzzing found this. No issue is filed.

title: bun:sqlite: refuse an asynchronous callback in db.transaction()
author: robobun
summary: Related to #24662 - `db.transaction(fn)` of `bun:sqlite` runs COMMIT when `fn` returns. An `async` callback returns at its first `await`, so later statements run outside the transaction. A failed transfer ends at `60, 0`, not `100, 0`. - Cause: `wrapTransaction` (`src/js/bun/sqlite.ts:670-674`) runs `after.run()` after `fn.$apply()`. It ignores the result.

title: fix(check): unify project ownership across paths and globals
author: vincentkoc
summary: A source listed by both a project and one of its references could be assigned to the project that redirects it, then skipped while `bun check` exited successfully. Directory requests could miss explicitly listed dot files, generated roots, or JavaScript projects. Fast inferred globals could choose a different project's options from the type checker. Named paths, directory roots, and fast globals now share the project-selection owner: prefer the first project in breadth-first reference order that

title: fix(check): preserve narrowed unions and mapped recursion identities
author: vincentkoc

author: vincentkoc
summary: Runtime `--check` did not consume or forward the checker controls accepted by `bun check`. For example, `bun --check --threads 2 --project selected.json app.ts` could resolve an option value as the entry point, while an equals-form thread control was ignored. Checker controls now share one parser/option owner across standalone checks, runtime checks, and CLI builds. The expanded parser activates only for an actual parsed `--check`; ordinary program arguments, Node aliases, Bunx, `--`, runtime `-

title: fix(ci): preserve test names without elapsed times
author: vincentkoc
summary: Preserves test names in the Node test runner when Bun omits the elapsed-time suffix. `lastIndexOf(" [")` returns `-1` for those lines, but the old truthiness check passed that index to `substring`, producing `"✓ "` or `"» "` instead of the name. Brackets within a name could also truncate it. The parser recognizes an anchored numeric duration suffix. title: node:assert: accept an empty message in `assert.throws` and `assert.rejects`
author: robobun
summary: - `assert.throws(fn, "")` and `assert.rejects(promise, "")` throw `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]: The argument 'error' may not be an empty object. Received ''`. A string in that position is the failure message. If nothing was thrown, the caller gets this `TypeError` in place of the `AssertionError`. Node v26.3.0 accepts `""`. - The cause is `expectsError` (`src/js/node/assert.ts:658`). In its `typeof error === "string"` branch it asks `Object.keys(error).length === 0`. Among strings, that is

title: webcrypto: compute hashes and symmetric ciphers over small inputs in the call
author: sosukesuzuki
summary: `crypto.subtle` sent every digest, HMAC and symmetric cipher operation to the thread pool. For a small input the trip costs far more than the work: an awaited `digest("SHA-256", 64 bytes)` takes about 20 µs, of which the hash is a fraction of a microsecond. Up to a size per algorithm, the operation now runs on the thread that called it. Its promise still settles from the event loop, on the next turn, as it does when the pool computed it. Larger inputs, and every other algorithm, go to the pool a

title: docs: correct the CSS math functions example and say where math is evaluated
author: robobun
summary: - The "Math functions" example in `docs/bundler/css.mdx` shows `--scale-factor: pow(1.25, 3)` printed as `--scale-factor: 1.953125`, and `transform: rotate(35.36deg)`. `bun build` prints `--scale-factor: pow(1.25, 3)` and `rotate(35.3553deg)`, in a different order. - The page says the bundler evaluates math "when all values are known constants". It does not say that this applies only to properties whose values Bun parses.

title: run: report a package.json that does not parse instead of using a parent's scripts
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #19604 - With a syntax error in `package.json`, `bun run <script>` prints only `error: Script not found "<script>"` and `bun run` prints `No package.json found.` If a package further up has that script, it runs instead, with exit 0. - Cause: `PackageJSON::parse` (`src/resolver/package_json.rs:406`) returned a bare `Option`. A file that did not parse was `None`, so the directory inherited its parent's `enclosing_package_json`.

title: node:test: port node's createSubtest argument shift into parseTestArgs
author: robobun
summary: - Under `bun test`, `node:test` drops the function of `test(undefined, fn)`, `test(42, fn)` and `test("name", undefined, fn)`. The test has no body and passes. Node v26.3.0 runs it. - Cause: `parseTestArgs` (`src/js/node/test.ts:1904`) set defaults inside the leaves of a `typeof` tree. Two leaves never read the later arguments.

title: bun build --production: write NODE_ENV after the process environment loads
author: robobun
summary: **Question for a maintainer:** does `bun build --production` outrank an exported `NODE_ENV` or `BUN_ENV`? This PR says yes. Nearest ruling: [#23821](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/23821#issuecomment-3424545722): the flag outranks tsconfig "since they're passing the CLI flag explicitly". - With `NODE_ENV=development` exported, `bun build --production` exits 0 and inlines `"development"`. It keeps development-only branches and emits `jsxDEV`. `bun build --app` does the same. - The flag wrote

title: node:http: give a request without a body its EOF at message-complete
author: robobun
summary: - A `node:http` request without a body that is paused before its first read never emits `'end'` or `'close'`. Since 1.4.3 (#43557), `req.pause()` in `'close'` of the response is enough. - hapi 21.4.10 adds `Connection: close` to each 401 for an empty POST: `req._readableState.ended` is false. - The server sets `req.complete` with no EOF (`src/js/node/_http_server.ts:1115`), and `_read()` queues it late. Not fixed: a chunked request with an empty body.

title: windows: commit one page of stack per thread and check the stack sizes of the linked exe
author: robobun
summary: - On Windows, a bun process near the commit limit ends when JSC starts a helper thread: `WTFCrashWithInfo` under `WTF::Thread::create`, exit code `0xC0000409` (561 Sentry events in 90 days). - The link flag `/STACK:0x1200000,0x200000` (`scripts/build/flags.ts:1020`) sets `SizeOfStackCommit`. Windows charges it when any thread starts, and refuses the thread when it cannot.

title: Bun.Image: write an ICC profile only when its header says RGB
author: robobun
summary: - `Bun.Image` writes a non-RGB ICC profile into RGB files. A greyscale PNG with a `GRAY` profile leaves `.png()` as colour type 6 with that profile. libpng warns `Gray color space not permitted on RGB PNG`. - A 557 KB `CMYK` profile on an RGB file makes a 128 px WebP thumbnail 558,552 bytes. This change makes it 1,358. - Decoders expand every source to RGBA8. `Image.rs:1739` passes the source profile to `codecs::encode` (#30197), which embeds it unread.

title: css: match named colors without regard to ASCII case
author: robobun
summary: - A named color with a capital letter does not parse. `Bun.color("Red", "hex")` is `null`. `@property --accent{syntax:"<color>";inherits:false;initial-value:White}` fails the build: `error: Unexpected token: White`. - `bun build` prints `.a{color:White}` as written, not as `#fff`. - The cause is `parse_named_color` (`src/css/css_parser.rs:5612`). `NAMED_COLORS.get(ident)` compares the bytes, and a CSS keyword is ASCII case-insensitive.

title: node:path: give posix and win32 matchesGlob their own memo, keyed on the raw pattern
author: robobun
summary: - `path.win32.matchesGlob("src\\x.js", "src\\*.js")` is `true`, then `false` after one `path.posix.matchesGlob(x, "src\\*.js")`. Node.js answers `true` both times. - Both flavours share one memoized `Bun.Glob` (`src/js/node/path.ts:50-76`). It compares the raw pattern, but stores the win32 one with `\` rewritten to `/`. So win32 reuses the posix glob, where `\` is an escape. - A win32 `\` pattern also never hits the memo: 500 calls build 500 globs.

title: css: allow `or` inside parentheses after a media type
author: robobun
summary: - `bun build` fails on the valid rule `@media screen and ((min-width: 600px) or (orientation: landscape))` with `error: Unexpected token: (`. It writes no file. - After a media type, `MediaQuery::parse` clears `ALLOW_OR` (`src/css/media_query.rs:1462`). That is correct. `parse_paren_block` (line 1596) passed the same flags into the parentheses and refused `or` there too.

title: Bun.CryptoHasher: accept a TypedArray of byteLength bytes in digest(hashInto)
author: robobun
summary: - `new Bun.CryptoHasher("sha256").digest(new Uint8Array(32))` throws `TypeError: TypedArray must be at least 64 bytes`. It is the example of `docs/runtime/hashing.mdx`. - 16 of the 19 algorithms refuse an array of their own `byteLength`. No user reported it. - `CryptoHasher::digest` (`src/runtime/crypto/CryptoHasher.rs:425`) gives `finish` `EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE` (64) as the minimum length of the array.

title: css: parse number and percentage channels in lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch(), hsl() and hwb()
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #16727 - `bun build` deletes a hand-written color fallback: `.x{color:red;color:oklch(0.5 0.1 40)}` builds to `.x{color:oklch(.5 .1 40)}`. `oklch(50% 0.1 40)` keeps both. - Each channel reader in `src/css/values/color.rs` takes one literal type. CSS Color 4 allows two. An unparsed `color` replaces the one before. - `Bun.color("lab(50% 50% 50%)")` is `null`, and such an `@property` `initial-value` fails the build.

title: bun test: on a timeout, kill only the processes the timed-out test or hook callback spawned
author: robobun
summary: - When one test times out, `bun test` kills every child process the file spawned: `killed 7 dangling processes` where the test spawned 1. - `Execution::kill_dangling_processes_on_timeout` (`src/runtime/test_runner/Execution.rs:324`) calls `auto_killer.kill()`, which drains the per-VM set. #22534 (1.2.23) dropped the per-test clear.

title: shell: record the last command substitution status per command and expand words first
author: robobun
summary: - `$(echo ./deploy.sh)` runs the script, then reports exit 0 when it exits 7. On piped stdio the shell also kills it at stdout EOF. `FOO=$(false)` always exits 0. - Causes: `Cmd::child_done` parked the `$(...)` status in `Cmd::exit_code` (`src/runtime/shell/states/Cmd.rs:379`), which `on_exit` reads as "the exec reported". `Assigns::next` returned 0 (`Assigns.rs:80`).

title: docs: say that --watch and --hot do not reach a package.json script
author: robobun
summary: - `docs/runtime/index.mdx:55` tells users to type `bun --watch run dev`. `dev` is a `package.json` script. `bun run` does not pass a `--watch` or `--hot` before the script name to the script, so the script runs once and nothing restarts it. - `docs/runtime/environment-variables.mdx:222` says that `BUN_OPTIONS="--hot"` makes `bun run dev` behave like `bun --hot run dev`. title: css: print the `=` comparison in media and container queries as `=`
author: robobun
summary: - `bun build` prints `@container (width = 500px)` as `@container (width - 500px)`, and as `@container (width-500px)` with `--minify`. Chrome 153 never applies a rule with either form. The build reports no error. - `@media (width = 500px)` prints the same way when the targets keep the range syntax (`--target=bun`, `--target=node`). - The cause is the `Equal` arm of `MediaFeatureComparison::to_css` (`src/css/media_query.rs:1030`). It writes `-`. lightningcss writes `=` there.

title: Worker: a preload that does not resolve throws the resolver's message again, not TypeError: undefined
author: robobun
summary: - `new Worker(entry, { preload: ["./missing.js"] })` throws `TypeError: undefined`. bun 1.3.14 throws `TypeError: BuildMessage: ModuleNotFound resolving "./missing.js" (entry point)`. - `WebWorker::create` (`src/jsc/web_worker.rs:307`) calls `transpiler.set_log(&raw mut temp_log)`, then moves `temp_log` into a scope guard. The resolver logs into the moved-from slot. The message is built from the copy in the guard. That copy is empty, so `Log::to_js` returns `undefined`.

title: Do not fail on a warning: gate Bun.Transpiler, FileSystemRouter and Worker on LogJsc::errors_to_js
author: robobun
summary: Supersedes #42433 and #42430. - `Bun.Transpiler` fails when its log holds only a warning (#7328, 2023). The four methods and the constructor throw a `BuildMessage` with `level: "warn"`: `Treating "-->" as the start of a legacy HTML single-line comment`. - 13 sites test "the log holds a message", not "the log holds an error": 11 in `src/runtime/api/JSTranspiler.rs`, `load_router` in `filesystem_router.rs`, and `flush_logs` in `web_worker.rs`. title: Do not glob an HTML entry path that names a file the glob cannot match
author: robobun
summary: - In `{guid}/app`, `bun ./index.html` exits 1 with `error: No HTML files found matching "/tmp/{guid}/app/index.html"`. With a second page, Bun serves only that page. Beside `a/app`, `{a,b}/app` serves the page of `a/app`. - `src/js/internal/html.ts:79` reads `process.argv[1]`, the resolved path, as a glob. `pages_of` in `check_command.rs` copies that test for `bun --check`.

title: node:http: an Upgrade request with a body follows Node v26
author: robobun
summary: - For an Upgrade request whose body came with its head, Node v26.3.0 gives the `'upgrade'` listener `req.complete === true`, the body in `req`, and the rest of the read as `head`. Bun gives `false` and both empty. A `socket.end()` in the listener loses the body and the tunnel bytes. - `onNodeHTTPRequest` (`src/js/node/_http_server.ts:1068`) emits at the end of the headers. `HttpContext::onData` (`packages/bun-uws/src/HttpContext.h:340`) drops the reads of a shut-down socket that is not yet a tun

title: node:http2: emit 'aborted' only while the writable side is open
author: robobun
summary: - `node:http2` emits `'aborted'` on a stream whose writable side ended. Node emits it only "if the `Http2Stream` writable side has not been ended". - A 204 after a consumed POST body always fires it, as does `end(body)` before a peer reset. bun 1.3.13 does neither. No user reported it. - The `aborted` handlers (`src/js/node/http2.ts:4072`, `:5078`) tested `old_state != 5 && old_state != 7`: the state of the wire.

author: steipete
summary: Preserve Windows device prefixes when splitting module queries. title: bun -e: keep the whole path of the entry module when the cwd has a `?`
author: robobun
summary: - In a cwd whose path has a `?` (POSIX, for example `/work/what?/`), a CommonJS `bun -e` or stdin script prints nothing and exits with 0. `bun -p "require('node:path').sep"` prints `[Function]`. - A dynamic `import("./config.json")` in the script loads the file of the folder before the `?`. - Cause: `get_loader_and_virtual_source` (`src/runtime/jsc_hooks.rs:3910`) cuts the entry key `<cwd>/[eval]` at the first `?`, as for a `?query`. author: robobun
summary: - `res.writeHead()` reads header values late, at the first `write()` or `end()`. When a handler gives one array to many responses, a client can receive the `Set-Cookie` of another user, or a CR LF value that `writeHead()` refused. Affected: 1.4.0 to 1.4.3. title: fix(run): point Node environment variables at shim executable
author: steipete
summary: Fixes `NODE` and `npm_node_execpath` when `bun run` selects its Node shim. author: steipete

author: steipete

author: steipete

The fixture first saves a session for `127.0.0.1`, then passes it to `tls.connect({ socket, session })` without a host. Inspector captures also miss the synchronous startup stack that Node records. With `BUN_GC_TIMER_DISABLE=1` the same code hangs until the test timeout. **Cause.** `.resolves`/`.rejects` wait for the promise synchronously (`src/runtime/test_runner/expect.rs:496` → `EventLoop::wait_for_promise`, `src/jsc/event_loop.rs:1129`), which loops `tick()` then `auto_tick()` (`event_loop.rs:1143`) while the promise is pending. `auto_tick

title: Bun.inspect.table: read the options after an `undefined` or `null` properties argument
author: robobun

title: node:http: emit 'close' on req.socket with hadError, also when its 'error' emit throws
author: robobun
summary: - `req.socket` never emits `'close'` when its `'error'` emit throws and an `uncaughtException` handler keeps the process alive. Since v1.4.3 (#43557) the response `'close'` is lost too. author: robobun
summary: - Since #41186 (1.4.1), `bun build` without `--splitting` gives wrong values. `import("./m.js").then(({ a }) => { if (no) { var a = 1 } console.log(a) })` logs `undefined`, not `"A"`. `const { a: x } = rest` off a `{...rest}` copy gives `"A"`. - A redeclared variable has two linked symbols, and `has_link()` (`src/js_parser/parse/parse_entry.rs:1533`) sees one end. `src/js_parser/visit/mod.rs:431` treats the copy as the namespace.

title: node:net: report a failed unix-socket connect on the next loop turn
author: robobun
summary: - Since 1.4.0 (#31587), requests through `http.Agent({ maxSockets: 1 })` to a `socketPath` with no listener never finish: main loops on uncaught `connect ENOENT`. author: robobun
summary: Fixes #4609 - A runtime `Bun.plugin` is silently skipped for `import("./a.ts?v=1.2.3")`, `./video.3gp`, `./a.ts?t=12:30` and files under `dir:name/`. title: node:http: make setKeepAlive() and the keepAlive option act on server sockets
author: robobun
summary: - `socket.setKeepAlive()` does nothing on the sockets of a `node:http` server, and `createServer({ keepAlive })` is ignored. `SO_KEEPALIVE` stays 0, so a peer that vanishes under an open response or a tunnel is never closed. - The cause is the stub `setKeepAlive()` of `NodeHTTPServerSocket` (`src/js/node/_http_server.ts:2145` on main). The server never reads the option.

title: fetch: reject a stream chunk that is not bytes or a string in blob() and formData()
author: robobun
summary: - `blob()` and `formData()` of `Response`/`Request` convert any chunk of a JS stream body to a string: `5` then `{}` resolves `"5[object Object]"`. The other four body methods refuse it. No user reported this. - Cause: `readableStreamToBlob` gives the chunk array to `new Blob(chunks)` (`BunStreamConsumers.cpp:1510`).

title: node:test run(): report child events in byte frames that printed text cannot produce
author: robobun
summary: - `run()` from `node:test` believes a string that a test prints. A logged line forges `test:pass`, `test:fail`, or an `end` that lets a script exit 0 over a failing test. - `handleStdoutLine` (`src/js/node/test.ts:512`, from #34444) searched decoded stdout for `\0bun:test:run\0` and emitted any `type`.

title: child_process: end the stdin pipe in child.stdin's _final
author: robobun
summary: - `child.stdin.end()` leaves the pipe open until `_destroy`, after the `end()` callback and the `'finish'` listeners. If one throws in a surviving parent, or waits for the child, the child gets no end-of-file. Node ends the pipe first. - `child.stdin` is an `fs.WriteStream` over a `FileSink` (`writableFromFileSink`, `src/js/internal/fs/streams.ts`) whose `_final` only flushes. Regression from 1.2.0 (#16422), no issue or report.

title: formData(): check the Content-Type before the lift that spends the .body stream
author: robobun
summary: - `const s = r.body; await r.formData()` on a body that is not form data rejects and leaves `s` locked while `r.bodyUsed` is false. `s.getReader()` throws `ReadableStream is locked`, and `Bun.write(path, r)` fails with `ERR_BODY_ALREADY_USED`. - Cause: `get_form_data` (`src/runtime/webcore/Body.rs`) calls `to_blob_if_possible()` before it looks at the Content-Type. Since #42516 that lift closes and locks the stream.

Only Linux agent time pays: 3.2%.

author: robobun
summary: - `bun init` writes two new-project defaults into a `package.json` that it loaded: `"type": "module"` and `"private": true`. It replaces `"commonjs"` and `false`, adds both keys when absent, prints nothing, and exits 0. - Then `node index.js` fails with `ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope`, and a Library-template package fails `bun publish` with `error: attempted to publish a private package`. - Cause: the two puts in `InitCommand::exec` (`src/runtime/cli/init_command.rs:6

title: Reset an inherited ignored SIGCHLD at startup on Linux
author: robobun
summary: - On Linux, bun started under a parent that ignores SIGCHLD loses every child's exit status. `Bun.spawnSync().exitCode` is `null`, `bun run` prints `ECHILD: No child processes (waitpid())` and exits 0 for a failed script, and `bun install` fails after a postinstall that ran. - An ignored SIGCHLD survives `execve`. Linux then reaps children itself, so `wait4()` fails. `main()` (`src/runtime/bin_entry/mod.rs:177`) sets only SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ. - No user reported this. It comes from a fuzz run.

title: tls: an empty `ca` list trusts no certificate
author: robobun
summary: - `ca: []` is read as "no `ca`": the context trusts the default roots. Node trusts no CA. On main a `{ ca: [], cert, key }` client completes mutual TLS. - `handle_file_array` (`src/runtime/socket/SSLConfig.rs`) returns `None` for an empty array, and `us_ssl_ctx_build_raw` (`openssl.c`) needs `ca_count > 0`.

title: test: keep isolation.test.ts and transpiler-cache.test.ts under their timeouts on debug builds
author: robobun
summary: Behaviour change: none - On a debug build, `bun bd test test/cli/test/isolation.test.ts` fails 2 of 3 runs. The child prints `(fail) A's FinalizationRegistry cleanup does not run here` and `this test timed out after 5000ms`. - `bun bd test test/cli/run/transpiler-cache.test.ts` fails 3 of 3 runs: `--define invalidates cache` and `--drop invalidates cache` print the same timeout. - Both are slow, not stuck. A child `bun test` keeps 5 s per test. A debug build takes 0.5 s to start a process, or 1.

title: bun:test: done(arg) fails the test only when the argument is truthy
author: robobun
summary: - The `done` callback of bun:test fails the test for every argument except `undefined` and `null`: `done(false)` prints `error: false`. Jest 30, Mocha 11 and `node:test` fail only on a truthy argument, so `socket.on("close", done)` passes there. - The cause is `let was_error = !value.is_empty_or_undefined_or_null();` in `bun_test_done_callback` (`src/runtime/test_runner/bun_test.rs:808`). title: Bun.write: do not chmod a FIFO or device destination when copying from Bun.file()
author: robobun
summary: - `Bun.write(dest, Bun.file(src), { mode })` changes the mode of a FIFO, device or terminal that exists at `dest`. On 1.4.2 a FIFO goes from 644 to 600. A script that writes to `/dev/stdout` changes the mode of its terminal. - `CopyFile::do_close` (`src/runtime/webcore/blob/copy_file.rs:184`) calls `fchmod` on the destination with no file-type check. #25906 added that call (v1.3.6).

title: node:http: complete a chunked request body before its last chunk is delivered
author: robobun
summary: - Since v1.4.3 (#43557), `server.close()` or `closeIdleConnections()` from the `'end'`, `'finish'` or `'close'` of a chunked request keeps its connection. `close()` waits `keepAliveTimeout` plus 1 s. Node and Bun 1.4.2 close at once. - In the last chunk's callback the parser state is `STATE_IS_TRAILERS_DONE` (`packages/bun-uws/src/ChunkedEncoding.h:256`). `closeIfIdle()` (`HttpResponse.h:167`) reads it as a body in progress.

title: process.stdout/stderr: emit 'close' on its own tick over a pipe, a socket or a TTY, as in Node
author: robobun
summary: - `process.stdout.destroy(err)` and `process.stderr.destroy(err)` emit no `'close'` when the `'error'` emit throws (no `'error'` listener, an `uncaughtException` handler). Node v26.3.0 emits it over a pipe, a stream socket and a TTY. Regression from #16422 (bun-v1.2.0). - Cause: the streams have `emitClose` on, so `emitErrorCloseNT` (`src/js/internal/streams/destroy.ts:116`) emits `'close'` after `'error'` in one tick. The throw skips it.

title: shell(touch): let the OS pick the time so that write access is enough
author: robobun
summary: - Bun's shell `touch` fails on a file that the caller can write but does not own: `touch: /dev/null: Operation not permitted`. coreutils `touch` succeeds. - Cause: `ShellTouchTask::run_from_thread_pool` (`src/runtime/shell/builtin/touch.rs:285`) read the clock and passed explicit times to `utimensat(2)`. Only the owner may set explicit times.

title: transpiler cache: treat an ES-module entry without a module record as a miss under test isolation
author: robobun
summary: - A run without isolation writes a transpiler cache entry with no module record. Each later `bun test --isolate` run parses that module once per test file. `bench/test/app`: 6,136 parses, not 2,632. - A type-only re-export then fails: `SyntaxError: export 'T' not found in './types'`. - Cause: an isolated reader takes the entry as a hit (`src/jsc/RuntimeTranspilerStore.rs:973`, `src/runtime/jsc_hooks.rs:2840`).

title: child_process: add setters for ChildProcess stdio and connected, return undefined before spawn
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44834 Supersedes #43008 and #43136. - `new ChildProcess().stdout` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'this.#handle')`. `child.stdout = new PassThrough()` throws `TypeError: Attempted to assign to readonly property.` in strict code. `ChildProcess.prototype.stdout` throws too. Node returns `undefined` (`false` for `connected`) and stores an assigned value. Test doubles built with `Object.assign(new ChildProcess(), { stdout, stderr })` fail on bun. - The cause: `stdin`

title: Bun.serve: share a route's payload with the Response's unread .body stream
author: robobun
summary: - After `const s = r.body` on a Response `r`, `Bun.serve({ routes: { "/a": r } })` leaves `s` locked while `r.bodyUsed` is false. `s.getReader()` throws `ReadableStream is locked`. `Bun.write(path, r)` fails with `ERR_BODY_ALREADY_USED`. So does a `Bun.file()` body (1.4.2 read the file). - Cause: `StaticRoute::from_js` and `FileRoute::from_js` call `to_blob_if_possible()` to look at the payload. Since #42516 that lift closes and locks the stream, and a route never reads it.

title: collections: grow a LinearFifo with one copy of the readable items and delete the scratch rotation
author: robobun
summary: - `ws.send()` blocks the JS thread for 12 s when a 16 MiB send queue that wraps around its buffer grows. A `Bun.serve` peer then closes the connection with 1006. - Since #22590 a grow first calls `realign()` on the old buffer (`src/collections/linear_fifo.rs:271`). For a queue that wraps, that moves the whole buffer once per 2048 bytes of `head`. - The JS task queue and the napi threadsafe-function queue have the same grow.

title: FormData: keep multipart parts whose name is empty
author: robobun
summary: - `formData()` drops a multipart part whose name is empty. `fd.append("", "v")`, then `await new Response(fd).formData()`, gives a form without that entry and no error. - The name is a `bun_semver::String`, which has one value for "empty" and "absent". So `for_each_multipart_entry` skips the part (`src/runtime/webcore/FormData.rs:380`).

title: test(node:http): measure the EPOLLHUP idle window again when teardown fills it
author: robobun
summary: - On a debug build this test can fail with an idle loop: "AF_UNIX CONNECT sockets whose peer closes first do not spin the loop on EPOLLHUP". At 71d0d43997, 2 of 30 runs printed `spun 524ms cpu in 1000ms`. - The fixture reports a spin at 500 ms of CPU in one 1000 ms window (`test/js/node/http/node-http-connect-unix-hangup-fixture.js:31`). The hangup closes the 8 server sockets inside it. A debug build spends 370 to 550 ms at 71d0d43997, 193 to 228 ms at 5f5799ed16.

title: sql: a closed pool connection hands its unsent requests back to the pool
author: robobun
summary: - When a pooled `Bun.SQL` connection closes, queries queued on it reject with `ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED` or `ERR_MYSQL_CONNECTION_CLOSED`. No byte of them was written. - `#finishClose` (`src/js/internal/sql/shared.ts`) and the driver cleanup (`clean_up_requests`, `MySQLRequestQueue::clean`) reject every request, written or not.

title: fs.promises: keep a FileHandle's descriptor open while an operation on it is pending
author: robobun
summary: - `fs.promises.readFile`, `writeFile` and `appendFile` use the descriptor number of a `FileHandle` with no ref (`src/js/node/fs.promises.ts:311`). `close()` or the finalizer closes it under the call. - `[kCloseSync]` (`:1494`), the close of an `autoClose` `writer()` or `pullSync()`, ignores the ref count. Four methods and the writer read arguments first.

title: Resolve setImmediate, clearImmediate and queueMicrotask in built-in modules to private names
author: robobun
summary: - Built-in modules call `setImmediate`, `clearImmediate` and `queueMicrotask` through the global object. When a program replaces them, as fake timers do, the runtime's own work is lost. A `PerformanceObserver`, `events.addAbortListener()` and `fs.watch()` never deliver, and a `node:http2` session never closes. - With the globals deleted: `ReferenceError: setImmediate is not defined` at `internal:shared`. Cause: 40 bare references in 11 `src/js` modules (`src/js/internal/shared.ts:394`).

title: docs: document the runtime transpiler cache location and the Windows Defender scan cost
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #44598 - On Windows, Defender real-time scanning of the runtime transpiler cache (`%USERPROFILE%\.bun\install\cache\@t@\*.pile`) makes `require("eslint-plugin-vue")` about 10x slower at times (400 ms to about 4 s). The reporter counted 1442 scans in one import. - The docs never name the cache directory, never mention Windows or antivirus, and do not say that `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` does not move this cache. A user cannot find the directory to exclude.

summary: Adds `bun patch-remove <pkg>[@<version>]` (accepts multiple packages), the counterpart of `bun patch --commit`: - removes the matching "patchedDependencies" entries from the root package.json (the field itself is dropped once empty), including when run from a workspace package - deletes the patch files and any patches directories they leave empty - reinstalls the affected packages unpatched and updates the lockfile through the

title: fix(ffi): convert int args instead of passing raw low 32 bits
author: MeGaurav4
summary: Small int FFI args skipped the JSVALUE_TO_INT32 conversion, so the raw int64 reached the C parameter and was truncated to its low 32 bits. That only works for int32-tagged values. Any double-encoded number arrived wrong: small integral doubles as 0, everything else as mantissa junk. All int args now go through the conversion, which handles both encodings. Only the trampoline codegen predicate and a regression test are changed, return paths untouched. Fixes #44906

title: js_parser: reject a modifier or an escape in front of a class static block
author: robobun
summary: Stacked on #44883. The diff is against its branch. - After a modifier or an escape, `static` before `{` is a member name. Bun runs `class A { async static {} }`, `static static {}` and `st\u0061tic {}`. V8 and JSC throw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '{'`. - TypeScript: `public static {}` runs the block and `declare static {}` deletes it. - Cause: the static block arm (`src/js_parser/parse/parse_property.rs:671`) tests only `{` and the name.

author: Neekoras
summary: `events.on` is missing from the browser polyfill, so the async-iterator form of consuming events throws in a browser bundle: ```js import { on, EventEmitter } from "node:events"; for await (const args of on(emitter, "message")) { // TypeError: on is not a function } ``` It is the only `node:events` export the polyfill lacks. This ports it from Bun's own `node:events`, with the two things a browser bundle cannot have taken out: - the JSC intrinsics (`Promise.$resolve`, `$makeAbortError`, `$ERR_IN

title: shell: keep an empty word that has a double-quoted expansion
author: robobun
summary: - A word with a double-quoted expansion that expands to nothing gives no argv word: `cmd "$UNSET"`, `cmd "$(true)"`. bash and dash pass one empty word. So `[ -n "$UNSET" ]` is true. - The lexer pushes the same `Token::Var` for `$X` and `"$X"` (`src/shell_parser/parse.rs:2652`). Only a literal `""` sets the flag that `Cmd::child_done` reads (`src/runtime/shell/states/Cmd.rs:390`).

title: tls: accept node's names for minVersion/maxVersion on TLS options, reject values that are not a version
author: robobun
summary: Related to #24214 - Since 1.4.0, `tls: { minVersion: "TLSv1.3" }` on `fetch`, `Bun.serve`, `Bun.listen` and `Bun.connect` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE TLSOptions.minVersion must be a number`. - A number that is not a protocol code is ignored. `0x10303` is applied as TLS 1.2. - Causes: both keys are `b.i32` (`SSLConfig.bindv2.ts:62`). `us_ssl_ctx_build_raw` drops the setter results and narrows to `uint16_t` (`openssl.c:1297`).

title: `bun check <file>`: check a file in the referenced project that lists it
author: robobun
summary: - `bun check vite.config.ts` prints `No type errors in 0 files` and exits 0 when the nearest `tsconfig.json` and a project it references both list the file. `bun --check <file>` then runs the file. - Cause: `Projects::find_project_with` (`src/sema/driver/lib.rs`) returns the nearest project first. That project reads the file through the declaration file of the referenced project, so no project checks it.

title: fetch: send an empty Bun.file() slice without sendfile and close its file
author: robobun
summary: - `fetch()` with the body `Bun.file(path).slice(0, 0)` leaks one file descriptor per call (file of 32 KiB or more, plain `http:`). At a limit of 4096 descriptors, upload 4,087 rejects with `EMFILE`. - `HTTPRequestBody::detach` (`src/runtime/webcore/fetch/FetchTasklet.rs:236`) closes the file only `if sendfile.offset.max(sendfile.remain) > 0`. An empty window (offset and length of the slice) at offset 0 has both at 0. - That window also calls `sendfile(2)` with length 0. macOS and FreeBSD read it

title: Bun.serve: keep idleTimeout armed while an HTTP/1 response write is blocked
author: robobun
summary: - `idleTimeout` never closes an HTTP/1 connection whose client sends a body and never reads a large response sent from memory. The client keeps the socket, the `Request` and `server.pendingRequests` with no bound. - Two lines turn the idle timer off while that write is blocked: `HttpResponse::pause()` (`packages/bun-uws/src/HttpResponse.h:554`) and the last body chunk (`packages/bun-uws/src/HttpContext.h:665`).

title: fetch, Bun.serve: stop dropping the body of a TRACE response
author: robobun
summary: Fixes #19615 - `fetch(url, { method: "TRACE" })` resolves with an empty body (`undici` and `node-fetch` shims too). If the body arrives after the next fetch took the pooled socket, that fetch rejects with `Malformed_HTTP_Response`. - A `Bun.serve` handler that answers TRACE with `Bun.file` sends `content-length: N` and 0 bytes. - Cause: `Method::has_body()` (`src/http_types/Method.rs:176`) excluded TRACE beside HEAD. The fetch client (`src/http/lib.rs:4952`, `:5351`) and `do_sendfile` (`src/runt

title: Blob: hand a file read to its consumer as owned bytes, so Bun.file().formData() frees it
author: robobun
summary: - `await Bun.file(path, { type }).formData()` never frees the bytes that it read. Memory grows by the size of the file on each call, on resolve and on reject. - `NewReadFileHandler::run` (`blob/read_file.rs:122`) gave its `Box<[u8]>` to `ReadFileToJs::call` as a raw pointer plus a `Lifetime` tag. The FormData consumer (`Blob.rs:5970`) has discarded the tag since #2051 and freed nothing.

title: node:http: a tunnel whose reads are stopped does not hold the event loop
author: robobun
summary: Fixes a regression from #43557 (in 1.4.3, not in 1.4.2): a `node:http` process never exits after `server.close()` while a CONNECT or Upgrade socket has its reads stopped. **Reproduction.** `test/js/node/http/node-http-connect-proxy-pipes-fixture.js` is the CONNECT proxy of the Node.js docs (`net.connect()` and two `pipe()` calls). Its upstream is slow and then goes away, its client gives up, and it calls `server.close()` with no `process.exit()`. | Runtime | Result | |---|---| | Node v22.22.0 |

title: js_parser: reject a decorator on a class static block, keep decorators out of the body of `declare global`
author: robobun
summary: - `class A { @dec(() => 0) static {} }` ends the process: `panic: Scope mismatch while visiting`. The static block arm (`src/js_parser/parse/parse_property.rs:671`) drops the decorators, so nothing visits their scopes. - `@dec(() => 0) declare global { declare const c: any }` ends it: `panic: range start index 3 out of range for slice of length 1`. Both `global` arms (`src/js_parser/parse/parse_stmt.rs:2942`, `:3017`) give the body the decorators of the statement.

title: bundler: give an explicit `define` precedence over `env` inlining of the same variable
author: robobun
summary: - Found by fuzzing, no user report. `bun build --define 'process.env.X="A"' --env inline` silently emits the environment's X when X is set. So do `--env 'PREFIX_*'`, `.env` files, `Bun.build`, macros and `Bun.serve` HTML routes without HMR. - Cause: `Define::init` (`src/bundler/defines.rs:205`) loads the `define` map, then the env entries. `DefineData::merge` keeps the later value.

title: node:http2: fail a dropped write with ECANCELED, keep no write callback in native
author: robobun
summary: Related to #40358 - A `node:http2` stream that ends with DATA frames queued drops them, and `Stream::clean_queue` (`src/runtime/api/bun/h2_frame_parser.rs:1910`) calls each write callback with no error. `write(cb)` and `pipeline()` report a dropped body as sent. - A write on a request with no stream id (`src/js/node/http2.ts:2927`) never calls back when the request ends first.

title: Bun.serve http2: close a connection gracefully with a FIN, not with close(2)
author: robobun
summary: - A graceful `server.stop()` on `Bun.serve({ http2: true })` cuts a response when the client sends a frame while it reads it. The client gets 1802126 of 4194304 bytes on h2c (2588604 over TLS), no GOAWAY, then a reset. - `Http2Context` calls close(2) as soon as its buffer is empty (`packages/bun-uws/src/Http2Context.h`, 7 sites). The kernel still holds the end of the response, and a client frame makes it reset the connection.

title: s3: report the name of the S3 file as `error.path` of every failed request
author: robobun
summary: Not a user report. Found during #44779. - `error.path` of a failed `s3.write("/the-key", data)` depends on the data. A string or a Blob gives none. `""` gives `"/the-key"`. `Bun.file(p)` gives `"the-key"`. A compiled executable gives the embedded name. - Cause: the single-PUT completion for in-memory data holds the source store (`src/runtime/webcore/Blob.rs:4552`). - `Store::get_path()` (`src/jsc/webcore_types.rs:921`) returns an S3 key as written. A streamed write reports `S3::path()`.

title: node:http: make res._send() the stored head plus _writeRaw(), as in Node.js
author: robobun
summary: - `res._send(data)` on a response queued behind a pipelined one loses `data` and the head of `writeHead()`. bun 1.4.2 threw an uncaught `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`. - `ServerResponse.prototype._send` (`src/js/node/_http_server.ts:3886`) writes to the handle at once. Only `write()`, `end()` and `_writeRaw()` know the queue. - `http.OutgoingMessage.prototype.end.call(res, chunk)` never ends a response.

title: sql: gate the values of unsafe() and file() on presence, not truthiness
author: robobun
summary: Draft, stacked on #44745 (the diff is against that branch, do not merge it there). **Open question:** is this the contract for a scalar `values`? Notes has two other answers. - A direct `sql.unsafe(text, values)` or `sql.file` takes a falsy non-array `values` (`0`, `false`, `""`) for "no values" and passes a truthy one to the adapter. SQLite stores NULL for `0` and 5 for `5`. - Cause: `values || []` in `normalizeQuery` (`src/js/internal/sql/shared.ts:399`). No user reported it.

title: run: export the project root as npm_config_local_prefix
author: robobun
summary: Part of #21088 Stacked on #44737: merge that first. - `bun run x` from `proj/sub/deep` exports `npm_config_local_prefix=proj/sub/deep`. npm exports `proj`, or the workspace root for a member. - The cause is `put_default(b"npm_config_local_prefix", top_level_dir)` in `configure_env_for_run_impl` (`src/runtime/cli/run_command.rs:682`). title: BUN_CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_HASHES: hash strings and numbers with secrets picked per process

author: robobun
